plains.text: Open grassland of the cold and temperate dry lands, full of herds. Groves of trees take patches of it.

savanna.text: Hot grassland with lone acacias, cattle, horses and goats. It never rains here.

shallow_ocean.text: The sea near the coast: reefs, seagrass and shoals of fish.

Rustcraft has no levels to grind: you get stronger by making better tools and armour, and the better materials lie deeper. The story ends at the bottom of the world, in the lair of the
. This page is the map of that road; each step links to the guide that covers it.

Every tool comes in each material. A pickaxe can only mine an ore if its tier is high enough: mined with a lower one, the block breaks and drops nothing. Speed is how many times faster than your bare hand it breaks the blocks it is made for.

Gold is the odd one: the fastest tool of all, but it wears out after 32 uses and mines only what wood mines. Bronze is a step between stone and iron: it mines the same ores as stone, but lasts longer and digs faster. Each pickaxe also mines everything the tiers under it mine.
Each point of armour takes 4 % off the blows of creatures, arrows, fire and lava. Falls, drowning, hunger and poison go through it. Every piece wears by 1 each time it softens a blow.
Each cell gives the armour points and the durability of the piece.

The world holds villages on the surface, three kinds of dungeon from the surface down to the lava, shipwrecks on the sea floor with treasure buried near them, and the lair of the Ember Mother. Their chests are filled when the world is generated.

Each chest and barrel has 27 slots. Every row of its table is rolled on its own: first the chance, then a count between the two numbers. A chest can hold many rows or none. What a container holds is fixed by the world's seed and its position.

There is at most one village in each 512 x 512 block area, with a chance of 4 in 5. A village needs dry, fairly flat land below height 76, well inside a biome that has a village style, away from giant jungle trees. It reaches at most 64 blocks from its centre.

Breaking it may give fibre, rye, a carrot or a potato: the start of every farm. See
Place it and use it for the 3 x 3 grid, which most recipes need; your inventory only has a 2 x 2 one. Having one earns
Smelts ores into ingots, cooks food and bakes sand into glass, one item every 10 seconds. It keeps working while you are away, as long as its chunk is loaded. Breaking it drops what is inside. See
Holds 27 slots. Breaking it drops what is inside. Put one on a tamed donkey or mule to make it a pack animal.
Breaking it gives flint one time in ten.
The first defence against the night: hostiles never spawn within 8 blocks of a light. Light your base and your mine.
Smelt iron ore for it; iron ore lies from y -24 to 72 in a new world and needs a stone or bronze pickaxe. Getting one earns
Found deep down: diamond ore lies from y -58 to 16 in a new world, most of it below -42. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better. See
Picks up a source of water or lava, and milks a cow. Only source blocks can be picked up: water that flows cannot.
Made from copper and tin. Bronze tools sit between stone and iron, and bronze armour between leather and iron: a good step before you find iron.
Use it to set your respawn point. At night, when every player online lies down, the night is skipped. If your bedroll is broken, you come back at the world spawn. Using one earns
Fills in the rain. Empty it with a bucket for a water bucket.
A light that keeps hostiles away and that rain puts out. Relight it with a torch, flint, or flint and steel.

The attack button opens your blue portal, the use button your orange one, on the face of a block up to 32 blocks away. A portal is 2 blocks wide and 3 high: its 6 wall cells must be solid full blocks (not glass or leaves) and nothing solid in the 6 in front of it. Walk into one and you come out of the other; you can see through them. A portal closes if its wall changes.
Made where a lava source meets water. Only a diamond pickaxe harvests it.
The best fuel of all: one burns for 1000 seconds, 100 items, and leaves its bucket.

text.text: The money of the villagers: sell them crops, coal, iron, fibre, feathers or leather for coins, and buy food, tools, armour and torches with them. See
Its needle points to the lair of the Ember Mother, at the bottom of the world. It spins in a world without one, and when you stand at the heart of the lair. Getting one earns
What the Ember Mother leaves when she falls: a block that glows with a light of 12. Only one is ever dropped per world.
Put it on a horse, donkey or mule you tamed, then use the animal to ride it. See
Put it on water and use it: 8 blocks a second on water, 1 on land, with a seat for a passenger in front.

Hold the use button to raise it: it stops the blows and arrows that come from the front, and you walk at half speed. A Roller’s charge or the Ember Mother’s blow knocks it down for five seconds. It works from any hotbar slot while your hand holds a melee weapon or nothing. See
Drink it to clear every status effect; the bucket is left. Get it by using a bucket on a cow.
Use it to start a map of the 128 x 128 blocks around you; it fills in as you walk, within 40 blocks of you. Copy a map by crafting it with an empty one.
Shows 128 x 128 blocks, a pixel each, and fills in within 40 blocks of whoever holds it. Hang it in a map frame, or copy it with an empty map.
Its needle points home: to your bedroll, or to the world spawn if you have none.
Use it on a crop to grow it a stage, on a berry bush to ripen it, or on a sapling for a one in two chance to grow it into a tree at once. See
Found in the chests of shipwrecks. While you hold it, your maps mark the spot of a buried chest with a red X, 24 to 72 blocks from the wreck. Dig 2 blocks down there. See
Use it on a land animal to lead it. The lead has 4 blocks of slack and snaps beyond 12; use it on a fence post to tie the animal there.
Fill it at a water source for a water vial, the start of every potion. See

behaviour.text: It runs from players. It eats berries, but cannot be tamed.

spawns.text: In herds of 1 to 2 in forests, groves and flower forests, and in the ice plains.

summary.text: A quick, shy animal of the woods and the snow.

behaviour.text: Use almost any item on an adult to shear it for 1 to 2 wool; the wool grows back once it has grazed. It eats rye.

spawns.text: In herds of 2 to 4 in the plains, groves, mountains and forests, and in the pens of plains and snowy villages.

summary.text: The source of wool and mutton.

behaviour.text: Use a
bucket
on an adult for a milk bucket, which clears every status effect. It eats rye.

spawns.text: In herds of 2 to 4 in the plains, the savanna, groves and forest clearings, and in village pens.

summary.text: Beef, leather and milk.

behaviour.text: It eats carrots and potatoes.

spawns.text: In herds of 2 to 4 in the plains and forests, and in plains village pens.

summary.text: An easy source of pork.

behaviour.text: An adult hen lays an
egg
about every five minutes. It eats rye.

spawns.text: In herds of 2 to 4 in the plains and forests, and in most village pens.

summary.text: Feathers, chicken, and eggs.

behaviour.text: It runs from players. It eats carrots.

spawns.text: In groups of 1 to 3 in the plains, flower plains, forest clearings and ice plains.

summary.text: A small, fast animal of the open land.

behaviour.text: Feed it meat, raw or roast: each time there is a one in three chance it becomes yours. A tamed wolf follows you, bites for 4 every second at what you hit and at the hostiles that go after you, and can be told to sit. See
taming

spawns.text: In packs of 2 to 4 in forests, groves and the ice plains.

summary.text: Tame one, and it fights at your side.

behaviour.text: Feed it carrots, rye or apples to tame it, put a saddle on it and ride. Each horse has its own speed, jump and endurance, read from its coat. See
riding

spawns.text: In herds of 2 to 4 in the plains, flower plains and the savanna.

summary.text: The fastest way across the land.

behaviour.text: It eats rye.

spawns.text: In herds of 2 to 4 in the mountains and the savanna, and in savanna and desert village pens.

summary.text: A hardy grazer of the heights and dry lands.

behaviour.text: Tame it with raw chicken or rabbit. A tamed cat follows you, and Gnawers and Gust Owls keep 8 blocks away from it.

spawns.text: In groups of 1 to 2 in forests, groves and forest clearings.

summary.text: Keeps the vermin away.

behaviour.text: It is weak alone but quick and comes in numbers. Its bite weakens you. It keeps away from a tamed cat. Its fang is the ingredient of the potion of strength.

spawns.text: In the dark underground below y 50, often in packs of 2 to 4, and as a guard of ruins and crypts.

summary.text: A cave rat that hunts in packs.

behaviour.text: It never moves: it waits for you to come within 2.5 blocks, then strikes and poisons you. Poison never kills, but leaves you at one point of health.

spawns.text: At night on grass in the woods, where it is one of two (with the Stumpling); as a guard of ruins.

summary.text: A bush that bites whoever comes close at night.

behaviour.text: It winds up for a second, then rolls at you at 7 blocks a second for up to three seconds, knocking you far back. If it hits a block, it is stunned for two seconds: that is the moment to strike. Its charge knocks a shield down.

spawns.text: Above y 100 in the mountains, and in the dark caves; as a guard of sanctuaries.

summary.text: A boulder that winds up and rolls at its prey.

behaviour.text: Its bark turns away blows from the front: an axe knocks its guard down for four seconds, and axes deal half again their damage to it. It flees fire and lava within 6 blocks, and it is the only hostile that opens doors.

spawns.text: At night on grass. It sinks back into the ground at dawn.

summary.text: A walking stump that comes out of the grass at night.

behaviour.text: It swims fast at you and grabs you: you are slowed and pulled down for two seconds, unable to swim up. On land it is slow and goes back to the water.

spawns.text: In water at least 3 blocks deep, at any hour: one time in four by day, one in two at night.

summary.text: A drowned thing that drags swimmers down.

behaviour.text: It floats 2 blocks up, keeps 6 blocks away from you and throws embers in arcs from up to 16 blocks. Embers set you burning and light what they land on. Water kills it, and so does rain on one under the sky: then it drops nothing.

spawns.text: In the dark of the Depths and below; summoned by the Ember Mother; as a guard of sanctuaries.

summary.text: A burning rock that hovers in the deep and throws embers.

behaviour.text: It circles 8 blocks above you, then dives from 6 to 10 blocks up at 10 blocks a second and knocks you back: dangerous on a cliff. It keeps away from a tamed cat.

spawns.text: At night under the open sky above y 110.

summary.text: An owl of the peaks that circles over its prey at night and dives.

behaviour.text: Villagers walk around their home by day and go in at night. Nothing hurts them and hostiles ignore them. Use one to trade. See
trading

spawns.text: In villages: each house gets one villager, the professions in turn.

summary.text: A villager who buys crops and sells food.

behaviour.text: Villagers walk around their home by day and go in at night. Nothing hurts them and hostiles ignore them. Use one to trade. See
trading

spawns.text: In villages: each house gets one villager, the professions in turn.

summary.text: A villager who buys coal and iron and sells tools and armour.

behaviour.text: Villagers walk around their home by day and go in at night. Nothing hurts them and hostiles ignore them. Use one to trade. See
trading

spawns.text: In villages: each house gets one villager, the professions in turn.

summary.text: A villager who sells torches, and tells where the nearest dungeon is.

behaviour.text: She throws volleys of embers and calls Cinderlings out of the lava; below half her health she charges, strikes hard and sets the floor on fire. She has 80 more health for each player after the first. See
the boss guide

spawns.text: Once per world, in her lair by the lava. She wakes when a player in survival enters it.

summary.text: The mother of the Cinderlings, asleep in her lair at the bottom of the world.

behaviour.text: It darts away when hurt.

spawns.text: In shoals of 3 to 6 over reefs and in water less than 10 deep.

summary.text: Small bright fish of the reefs, in shoals.

behaviour.text: It darts away when hurt.

spawns.text: In shoals of 3 to 6 in the open sea.

summary.text: Silver fish of the open sea, in shoals.

behaviour.text: It never attacks. Its moss makes potions last longer at the alembic.

spawns.text: In the lush caves of the deep, with its chunk.

summary.text: A slow shelled grazer of the damp caves, its back grown with moss.

behaviour.text: It pinches and knocks you back. Its shards make potions stronger at the alembic.

spawns.text: In the crystal caves of the deep, with its chunk, and in the dark on geodestone.

summary.text: A crab of crystal that guards the crystal caverns.

behaviour.text: Its bite sets you burning. Fire resistance spares you the burn, not the bite.

spawns.text: In the dark on basalt or magma, in the basalt galleries of the deep.

summary.text: A crawler of slag from the basalt galleries.

behaviour.text: Tame it like a horse. It is slower but lasts longer at a gallop, and with a chest on its back it carries 27 slots. With a horse, it breeds a mule.

spawns.text: In groups of 1 to 3 in the plains.

summary.text: A steady steed that carries a chest.

behaviour.text: It carries a chest like the donkey, and never breeds.

spawns.text: Never in the wild: breed a horse with a donkey.

summary.text: Born of a horse and a donkey.
